notes: Lead: Head of Product (Sami Ortega) — evaluating Hosted API for 3-week trial; moved to Dedicated sizing after throughput/PTL tests. Hosted trial summary: default gpt-like open weights, 6000 reqs/day, avg tokens per request ~480 (input 160 / output 320). Observed 70% of sessions short QPS (<128 tokens) and 30% long-form (>512 tokens). Latency target: 150-250ms p50 for short chat; will accept 300-450ms for long generations. Cost sensitivity: medium-high — concerned about token spend during nightly batch summarization run. POC results (11/23 demo): 1) prefix caching cut 30% of repeat tokens on FAQ flows; 2) concurrency spikes during morning digest cause tail latency to spike. Requested dedicated sizing worksheet: baseline steady QPS 20, expected business hours peak QPS 85, burst-safe up to 220 QPS for 10-15min windows. Concurrency target: sustain 60 concurrent streams with KV cache warm. Token mix: estimate 65% short (<128), 25% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512). Autoscale preference: mix of steady reserved plus burst buffer (prefer 2:1 spot/burst policy). Routing/fallback: prefer primary high-quality model with automatic fallback to quantized variant on capacity constraints. Security: must support SSO/SAML, enterprise KMS, audit logs and 90-day retention; data residency: prefer US and EU options for regional customers. Quotes: 'need predictable monthly commit, can't accept pay-as-you-go surprises' (Sami). Pricing conversation notes: AE provided draft reserved tiers; looking for a 12-month committed tier with 3-month ramp. Legal ask: standard DPA + SOC2 attestation; procurement wants SLA 99.9% for p50 latency and capacity. Next steps: pricing call 12/04, send final capacity worksheet and cost-per-token bakeoff, legal to receive SOW. POC Jira: RED-3421 open for cache anomalies; engineering asked for token-level telemetry (request/response token histograms).
